title: MATH2010 Module 03: Solution Sets & Linear Independence

questions.q: A homogeneous system of linear equations Ax = 0 can be inconsistent.
questions.explain: Setting every variable to 0 makes every equation read 0 = 0, so the zero vector is always a solution. A homogeneous system is always consistent. The real question is whether it has a solution other than x = 0.

questions.q: Which of these systems are homogeneous?
choices: x₁ - 3x₂ = 0 and 2x₁ + x₂ = 0
x₁ - 3x₂ = 0 and 2x₁ + x₂ = 4
x₁ = 3x₂ and x₂ = -x₃
x₁ + x₂ = 1 + x₃ and x₁ - x₃ = 0
questions.explain: A system is homogeneous if it can be written as Ax = 0. Moving terms over, x₁ = 3x₂ and x₂ = -x₃ become x₁ - 3x₂ = 0 and x₂ + x₃ = 0, so that system is homogeneous. The second system has a 4 on the right. The fourth becomes x₁ + x₂ - x₃ = 1. Both of those are non-homogeneous.

questions.q: A homogeneous system in x₁, x₂, x₃ has a coefficient matrix whose echelon form has rows [1, 4, -2], [0, 3, 5], [0, 0, 7]. What is its solution set?
choices: Infinitely many solutions, including non-zero ones
Only the zero solution x = 0
No solutions, because the system is inconsistent
Exactly one non-zero solution
questions.explain: There is a pivot in every column, so there are no free variables. A homogeneous system has a non-zero solution only if it has a free variable, so the only solution is x = 0. It can't be inconsistent, because x = 0 always works.

questions.q: A homogeneous system in x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ has a coefficient matrix that row reduces to rows [1, 2, 0, -1], [0, 0, 1, 3], [0, 0, 0, 0]. Which statement is correct?
choices: It has only the zero solution, because the last row is all zeros
It has a non-zero solution, because x₁ and x₃ are free
It has a non-zero solution, because x₂ and x₄ are free
It is inconsistent, because the last row is all zeros
questions.explain: The pivots are in columns 1 and 3, so x₁ and x₃ are basic and x₂, x₄ are free. Having at least one free variable means a non-zero solution exists. In a homogeneous system a zero row just says 0 = 0. It does not make the system inconsistent.

questions.q: If the coefficient matrix of Ax = 0 has a pivot in every column, then Ax = 0 has a non-zero solution.
questions.explain: A pivot in every column means there are no free variables. A homogeneous system has a non-zero solution if and only if it has at least one free variable, so here x = 0 is the only solution.

questions.q: Complete the theorem: a homogeneous system Ax = 0 has a non-zero solution if and only if...
choices: the system has at least one free variable
the right-hand side is not the zero vector
the echelon form of A has a row of zeros
A has more rows than columns
questions.explain: The non-zero solution comes from choosing a free variable to be non-zero. A zero row does not guarantee a free variable: a 4 × 3 matrix can have a zero row and still have a pivot in every column. Having more rows than columns does not force a free variable either. A non-zero right-hand side would make the system non-homogeneous.

questions.q: A homogeneous system in x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ has a coefficient matrix whose reduced echelon form has rows [1, 0, -3, 0], [0, 1, 2, 0], [0, 0, 0, 1]. What is its solution set?
questions.explain: The pivots are in columns 1, 2 and 4, so only x₃ is free. Solving gives x₁ = 3x₃, x₂ = -2x₃ and x₄ = 0, so x = x₃(3, -2, 1, 0). Moving -3x₃ and 2x₃ to the right-hand side flips their signs. The x₄ entry must be 0 because x₄ is basic, not free. The vector has 4 entries because there are 4 variables.

questions.q: The augmented matrix of a system in x₁, x₂, x₃, x₄ has reduced echelon form with rows [1, -2, 0, 4 | 3] and [0, 0, 1, -1 | 5]. Which is the solution set in parametric vector form?
questions.explain: x₁ and x₃ are basic, and x₂ and x₄ are free. Solving gives x₁ = 3 + 2x₂ - 4x₄ and x₃ = 5 + x₄. The typical solution is (3 + 2x₂ - 4x₄, x₂, 5 + x₄, x₄), which splits into (3, 0, 5, 0) + x₂(2, 1, 0, 0) + x₄(-4, 0, 1, 1). The span answer is wrong because the system is non-homogeneous, so x = 0 is not a solution.

questions.q: Find the solution set of the homogeneous system x₁ + 2x₂ + 3x₃ = 0, 2x₁ + 5x₂ + 4x₃ = 0.
choices: Only the zero vector
questions.explain: R₂ - 2R₁ gives [0, 1, -2]. Then R₁ - 2R₂ gives [1, 0, 7]. So x₁ = -7x₃ and x₂ = 2x₃ with x₃ free, and x = x₃(-7, 2, 1). Check: -7 + 4 + 3 = 0 and -14 + 10 + 4 = 0. The free variable's own row (x₃ = x₃) puts a 1 in the third entry, not a 0.

questions.q: To write a solution set in parametric vector form, you split the typical solution into a linear combination of constant vectors. In one word, what role do the free variables play in that linear combination?
questions.explain: The free variables are the weights: x = x₂u + x₄w + ..., where u and w are constant vectors (vectors whose entries are just numbers).

questions.q: A homogeneous system in x₁, ..., x₅ has a coefficient matrix whose echelon form has pivots in columns 1, 2 and 4. If you write its solution set as Span{...} using the parametric vector form procedure, how many vectors are inside the span?
questions.explain: Columns 3 and 5 have no pivot, so x₃ and x₅ are free. Each free variable contributes one constant vector, so the span contains 2 vectors.

questions.q: If the reduced echelon form gives the equation x₄ = 0, then x₄ is a free variable, since no other variable appears in its equation.
questions.explain: A variable is free only when its column has no pivot. If the reduced echelon form produces x₄ = 0, column 4 has a pivot, so x₄ is basic and equals 0. That 0 must appear in the x₄ entry of the solution vector.

questions.q: A system's solutions are x₁ = 3 - 2x₃, x₂ = 1 + 5x₃, with x₃ free. Which describes the solution set in R³?
choices: The line through (3, 1, 0) parallel to (-2, 5, 0)
The line through the origin parallel to (-2, 5, 1)
The line through (3, 1, 0) parallel to (-2, 5, 1)
The plane Span{(3, 1, 0), (-2, 5, 1)}
questions.explain: x = (3 - 2x₃, 1 + 5x₃, x₃) = (3, 1, 0) + x₃(-2, 5, 1). The third row is x₃ = x₃, which puts a 0 in the constant vector and a 1 in the direction vector. The line does not pass through the origin, so it is not a span.

questions.q: The solution set of a consistent non-homogeneous system Ax = b is the span of some set of vectors.
questions.explain: A span always contains the zero vector, but x = 0 does not solve Ax = b when b ≠ 0. The solution set has the form p + (span of the homogeneous solution vectors), which is a translated line or plane.

questions.q: Ax = b, with b ≠ 0, is consistent and has solutions x = p + t v (t any real number). Ax = 0 has solution set Span{v}. How do the two solution sets compare geometrically?
choices: They are the same line through the origin
They are parallel lines: the Ax = b line is the Ax = 0 line translated by p
They are lines that cross at the point p
The Ax = b solution set is the plane Span{p, v}
questions.explain: Both systems have the same coefficient matrix A, so they have the same free variables and the same direction vector v. The Ax = 0 line passes through the origin and the Ax = b line passes through p. Since b ≠ 0, the origin is not on the Ax = b line, so the two lines are parallel and distinct.

questions.q: A homogeneous system in x₁, x₂, x₃ has exactly two free variables. Geometrically, its solution set is:
choices: a line through the origin
a plane that does not pass through the origin
a plane through the origin
the single point 0
questions.explain: Each free variable gives one constant vector, so the solution set is the span of two vectors. In R³ that is a plane. Because it is a span, it contains the origin.

questions.q: Ax = b is consistent, p = (1, 0, 2) is one solution of it, and the solution set of Ax = 0 is Span{(1, 1, 0)}. Which vectors are also solutions of Ax = b?
questions.explain: The solutions of Ax = b are p plus the solutions of Ax = 0: (1, 0, 2) + t(1, 1, 0) = (1 + t, t, 2). Taking t = 0, 2 and -1 gives (1, 0, 2), (3, 2, 2) and (0, -1, 2). The vector (1, 1, 0) solves Ax = 0, not Ax = b. Neither (0, 0, 0) nor (2, 1, 4) has third entry 2.

questions.q: Which describes the solution set of the single equation x₁ - x₂ + 2x₃ = 4 in R³?
choices: x = (4, 0, 0) + x₂(1, 1, 0) + x₃(-2, 0, 1), a plane through (4, 0, 0) that does not contain the origin
x = (4, 0, 0) + x₂(1, 1, 0) + x₃(-2, 0, 1), a plane through the origin
questions.explain: x₁ is basic and x₂, x₃ are free, with x₁ = 4 + x₂ - 2x₃. Splitting (4 + x₂ - 2x₃, x₂, x₃) gives (4, 0, 0) + x₂(1, 1, 0) + x₃(-2, 0, 1). Two free variables give a plane. It is the plane Span{(1, 1, 0), (-2, 0, 1)} (the solutions of x₁ - x₂ + 2x₃ = 0) shifted by (4, 0, 0), so it misses the origin.

questions.q: By definition, a set {v₁, ..., vᵣ} in Rⁿ is linearly independent when the vector equation x₁v₁ + ... + xᵣvᵣ = 0...
choices: has the zero solution
has at least one non-zero solution
has only the zero solution x₁ = ... = xᵣ = 0
has no solution
questions.explain: The equation always has the zero solution, so 'has the zero solution' tells you nothing. Independence means the zero solution is the only one. Having a non-zero solution means the set is dependent. 'No solution' is impossible, since x = 0 always works.

questions.q: If {v₁, v₂, v₃} is linearly dependent, then v₁ must be a linear combination of v₂ and v₃.
questions.explain: The theorem only guarantees that at least one vector is a combination of the others. Example: v₁ = (1, 0), v₂ = (0, 1), v₃ = (0, 2). The set is dependent because v₃ = 2v₂, but v₁ is not a combination of v₂ and v₃.

questions.q: A set of vectors is linearly dependent if and only if at least one of the vectors in the set is a linear combination of the others.
questions.explain: If x₁v₁ + ... + xᵣvᵣ = 0 with some xⱼ ≠ 0, divide by xⱼ to solve for vⱼ in terms of the others. Conversely, if vⱼ is a combination of the others, moving it to the other side gives a dependence relation with weight -1 on vⱼ.

questions.q: Vectors v₁, v₂, v₃ satisfy 2v₁ - 3v₂ + v₃ = 0. Which statement is correct?
choices: The set is linearly independent, since the weights are not all zero
The set is linearly dependent, and v₃ = 2v₁ - 3v₂
The set is linearly dependent, and v₃ = -2v₁ + 3v₂
You cannot decide without knowing the entries of the vectors
questions.explain: Weights that are not all zero and combine the vectors to 0 form a linear dependence relation, so the set is dependent. Solving for v₃ gives v₃ = -2v₁ + 3v₂.

questions.q: Vectors v₁, v₂, v₃ satisfy 2v₁ - 3v₂ + v₃ = 0. If you write v₁ = a·v₂ + b·v₃, what is a? (Enter a decimal.)
questions.explain: 2v₁ = 3v₂ - v₃, so v₁ = 1.5v₂ - 0.5v₃. You can solve for any vector whose weight in the relation is non-zero.

questions.q: If x₁ = x₂ = x₃ = 0 is a solution of x₁v₁ + x₂v₂ + x₃v₃ = 0, then {v₁, v₂, v₃} is linearly independent.
questions.explain: The zero solution works for any set of vectors. Independence requires it to be the only solution.

questions.q: To test whether {v₁, ..., vᵣ} is linearly independent, what should you row reduce, and what should you look for?
choices: The matrix with v₁, ..., vᵣ as its rows; look for a row of zeros
The matrix [v₁ ... vᵣ] with the vectors as columns; look for a pivot in every column
The augmented matrix [v₁ ... vᵣ | 0]; look for a row [0 ... 0 | c] with c ≠ 0
The matrix [v₁ ... vᵣ] with the vectors as columns; look for a pivot in every row
questions.explain: The equation x₁v₁ + ... + xᵣvᵣ = 0 is the matrix equation Ax = 0 with A = [v₁ ... vᵣ]. The columns are independent exactly when Ax = 0 has only the zero solution, which means no free variables, which means a pivot in every column. A homogeneous system never has an inconsistent row.

questions.q: The set {(1, 2, 0), (0, 1, 3), (2, 5, 4)} is linearly independent.
questions.explain: Put the vectors in as columns: rows [1, 0, 2], [2, 1, 5], [0, 3, 4]. R₂ - 2R₁ gives [0, 1, 1]. Then R₃ - 3R₂ gives [0, 0, 1]. There is a pivot in every column, so there are no free variables. Ax = 0 has only the zero solution, so the set is independent.

questions.q: Let v₁ = (1, 2, 0), v₂ = (0, 1, 3), v₃ = (2, 5, 3). Which is a linear dependence relation for {v₁, v₂, v₃}?
choices: v₁ + 2v₂ - v₃ = 0
2v₁ - v₂ - v₃ = 0
None exists, because the set is linearly independent
2v₁ + v₂ - v₃ = 0
questions.explain: [v₁ v₂ v₃] reduces to rows [1, 0, 2], [0, 1, 1], [0, 0, 0]. Column 3 has no pivot, so x₃ is free and the set is dependent. From the reduced form, x₁ = -2x₃ and x₂ = -x₃. Taking x₃ = -1 gives 2v₁ + v₂ - v₃ = 0. Check: (2, 4, 0) + (0, 1, 3) - (2, 5, 3) = (0, 0, 0).

questions.q: For what value of k is the set {(1, 3), (k, 6)} linearly dependent?
questions.explain: Row reduce the matrix with rows [1, k], [3, 6]. R₂ - 3R₁ gives [0, 6 - 3k]. Column 2 has no pivot exactly when 6 - 3k = 0, so k = 2. Then (2, 6) = 2(1, 3).

questions.q: Let v₁ = (1, 0, 2), v₂ = (2, 1, 3), v₃ = (0, 1, h). For what value of h is {v₁, v₂, v₃} linearly dependent?
questions.explain: [v₁ v₂ v₃] has rows [1, 2, 0], [0, 1, 1], [2, 3, h]. R₃ - 2R₁ gives [0, -1, h]. Then R₃ + R₂ gives [0, 0, h + 1]. Column 3 has a pivot unless h + 1 = 0. So the set is dependent only when h = -1, and then v₃ = -2v₁ + v₂. For every other h it is independent.

questions.q: Four vectors v₁, v₂, v₃, v₄ in R³ are placed as the columns of A. An echelon form of A has rows [2, 1, 0, 3], [0, 0, 4, 1], [0, 0, 0, 5]. What can you conclude?
choices: Independent, because every row has a pivot
Dependent, because column 2 has no pivot
Independent, because there is no row of zeros
Dependent, because column 4 has no pivot
questions.explain: The pivots are 2 (column 1), 4 (column 3) and 5 (column 4). Column 2 has no pivot, so x₂ is free and Ax = 0 has non-zero solutions. The columns are dependent. Independence needs a pivot in every column, not in every row.

questions.q: To decide whether b is in Span{v₁, ..., vᵣ}, you should:
choices: Row reduce the augmented matrix [v₁ ... vᵣ | b] and check whether the system is consistent
Row reduce [v₁ ... vᵣ] and check for a pivot in every column
Check whether b is a scalar multiple of v₁
Row reduce [v₁ ... vᵣ | b] and check for a pivot in every column of the augmented matrix
questions.explain: b is in the span exactly when x₁v₁ + ... + xᵣvᵣ = b has a solution, which means the augmented system is consistent (no row [0 ... 0 | c] with c ≠ 0). A pivot in the last column of the augmented matrix means the system is inconsistent, so b is NOT in the span. Checking for a pivot in every column of [v₁ ... vᵣ] tests independence, which is a different question.

questions.q: For what value of h is b = (3, 1, h) in Span{(1, 0, 2), (0, 1, -1)}?
questions.explain: The augmented matrix has rows [1, 0 | 3], [0, 1 | 1], [2, -1 | h]. R₃ - 2R₁ gives [0, -1 | h - 6]. Then R₃ + R₂ gives [0, 0 | h - 5]. The system is consistent only when h = 5. Check: 3(1, 0, 2) + 1(0, 1, -1) = (3, 1, 5).

questions.q: Let A have rows [1, 2, 0], [0, 1, 1], [1, 3, 1], and let v = (1, 1, 3). Is v in the span of the columns of A?
choices: Yes, because any three vectors in R³ span all of R³
No, because the columns of A are linearly independent
Yes, because the reduced augmented matrix has a row of zeros
No, because [A | v] reduces to a matrix with the row [0, 0, 0 | 1], so Ax = v is inconsistent
questions.explain: [A | v] has rows [1, 2, 0 | 1], [0, 1, 1 | 1], [1, 3, 1 | 3]. R₃ - R₁ gives [0, 1, 1 | 2]. Then R₃ - R₂ gives [0, 0, 0 | 1], which says 0 = 1, so v is not in the span. The columns of A are actually dependent: column 3 has no pivot, and col₃ = col₂ - 2col₁. So they span only a plane through the origin, and v is not on that plane.

questions.q: Let A have rows [1, 2, 0], [0, 1, 1], [1, 3, 1]. The vector w = (1, 1, 2) is in the span of the columns of A.
questions.explain: [A | w] has rows [1, 2, 0 | 1], [0, 1, 1 | 1], [1, 3, 1 | 2]. R₃ - R₁ gives [0, 1, 1 | 1]. Then R₃ - R₂ gives [0, 0, 0 | 0]. There is no inconsistent row, so the system is consistent. For example, taking x₃ = 0 gives w = -col₁ + col₂ = -(1, 0, 1) + (2, 1, 3).

questions.q: Any three vectors in R³ span all of R³.
questions.explain: If the vectors are dependent, one of them is redundant and they span less. Example: (1, 1, 2), (0, 1, 1) and (1, 0, 1) satisfy (1, 0, 1) = (1, 1, 2) - (0, 1, 1). They span only a plane through the origin, and (1, -1, 2) is not in their span.

questions.q: The span of any set of vectors contains the zero vector.
questions.explain: Choose every weight to be 0: 0·v₁ + ... + 0·vᵣ = 0. This is why the solution set of Ax = b with b ≠ 0 can never be a span.
